Massive win for the Zimbabwean team as they win by 99 runs. Mustafizur Rahman c and b Brad Evans 6(6) [6s-1]

22:35 Local Time, 18:35 GMT, 00:05 IST: Zimbabwe have notched up a massive win. Bangladesh would be gutted. They had Zimbabwe on the ropes when they started bowling. But Taylor and Ervine rebuilt it and managed to help their team get beyond 270. Bangladesh with the bat never were in the chase with the bat barring the first 10 overs. Post that they kept losing wickets at regular intervals and in the end fell short by a huge margin. Evans was the pick of the bowlers and picked up four wickets. The spinners - Raza and Muzarabani - also snared up 2 wickets apiece. Bangladesh will want to go back to the drawing board as far as their batting is concerned. Zimbabwe will welcome the points and the massive face lift to their NRR.

Brad Evans: Nice to finish in that way. Tanzid has had the better of us in the last few white-ball series, he's a good player and tough to bowl at. But I think the message we had in the change room was to give your best. You never know what happens in white-ball cricket, the ball flies. Just gave our own and came up best. (On Shanto's dismissal) Nice ball, I don't know why he sent it upstairs. It was nice to come back like that, I just tried to hit the wicket and it paid off. (On the off-field camaraderie) Cricket is all about partnerships: batting, bowling and even fielding. We're great mates in that dressing room, always supporting each other's backs, whenever we bowl or bat, we do it for each other. (on Sikandar Raza's first win as ODI captain) We might have some beers in the change room, but we'll be back in the middle in two day's time.

Raza (3/3): And if we have won today, hopefully this is a start of many more wins to come. And regardless of whether I’m the captain or Richard (Ngarava) is the captain, when we put on this jersey, the aim is to win, regardless of who’s leading the side. So this win is as good as the other wins that other captains have got, and I’ve been part of it. So a win is something that we enjoy and we take a lot of pride in enjoying. [On the conditions] I think this is our first tour to the subcontinent in this weather. And I think the weather has hit us hard. I think it’s going to come down to mental toughness and discipline from all of us together. We’re going to have to pull each other, help our teammates to do the right things, because in the next 36 hours, not even 36 hours, we’ll be back here trying to put everything on the line for our country. So it’s very important that we do the right things. Keep your voice, get that body right.
Bangladesh have been left with a lot of questions. But we feel we have answered your questions about this game. We will be back soon with more cricketing action soon. Bye for now.
